events.description: Crafting Resilience: Finding Community and Connection through Fiber Arts is an artist-led workshop where participants gather together — without technology — to build community while working on a fiber craft of their choosing. Bring your own project that’s in process or start a new one with materials and tools provided; we’ll be working primarily in knitting, crochet, needle-felting, and embroidery. Stop by or stay for the whole time: we’ll get to know each other and share ways that we’re practicing resilience together and on our own. From novice to expert, everyone is welcome and demonstrations will be available for those looking to learn. Light snacks and refreshments provided. This workshop is led by FAM Collections Manager Krista Anderson-Larson and made possible by funding from the Gimse Striving for Peace on Horizon’s Brim Art Endowment.
events.title: Crafting Resilience: Finding Community and Connection through Fiber Arts

events.description:
Daily Chapel is a time of inspiration for body, mind, and spirit; a quiet harbor in a busy day; worship. Students, faculty, and staff witness to their faith and invite the community to join them. All are welcome!

This year’s service will include the awarding of the Founders Medal, which recognizes recipients as modern founders of the college. The award serves as a public declaration of deep gratitude from the entire St. Olaf community, highlighting the transformative power of philanthropy in supporting higher education.

The Founders Medal is amongst the highest honors the college can bestow, recognizing individuals whose extraordinary contributions have significantly advanced the college’s mission and improved the lives and outcomes of St. Olaf students today and for centuries to come. The recipient of this year’s Founders Medal are O. Jay and Pat Tomson.

All are invited to a reception in the King’s Dining Room following the chapel service.

If you are unable to join us in person but would like to watch live or archived chapel services, please click the web link below.

events.description:
24th Sunday after Pentecost; Sunday Worship with Holy Communion

The preacher today will be Associate College Chaplain Sarah Semmler Smith ’04;  presided by College Chaplain Matthew Marohl and assisted by Jonathan Madden ’20, Interim Cantor to the Student Congregation. The Manitou Singers will be conducted by Therees Hibbard, Associate Professor of Practice and Robert Scholz Endowed Chair in Music. Comprised of alto and soprano voices from the first-year class, the Manitou Singers is one of the most popular music organizations on the St. Olaf College campus. With a repertoire that ranges from sacred to secular to popular ballads, the 100-voice choir sings at the opening worship service of the college as well as at various campus functions throughout the year.

Sunday Worship is a time of inspiration and worship for body, mind, and spirit; a meaningful beginning to a new week. All are welcome!

Click the web link below to access streamed and archived services.
events.title: Sunday Morning Worship: 24th Sunday after Pentecost
